title: Introduce transient schema adapter to smooth schema deprecations for streaming tool-calls
author: Sana Kaur
release_notes: Adds a transient adapter middleware that rewrites incoming requests and outgoing streaming envelopes to maintain compatibility across schema deprecations. Ships behind opt-in header; no default behavior change.
description:
Motivation:
We are rolling schema changes for tool/function call envelopes and streaming structured output (v1 -> v2). Customers running older clients observed breaking changes when servers started to emit v2 streaming frames. This PR adds a transient-schema-adapter middleware in the OpenAI-compat proxy to smooth deprecations with three goals: 1) preserve streaming stability for mixed client fleets, 2) avoid long-lived hacks in customer code by exposing an opt-in compatibility header, and 3) emit telemetry to measure client-side adoption so we can retire shims safely.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces pkg/compat/adapter: a middleware that performs request rewriting and incremental response coercion for streaming tool responses. The adapter can coerce field names, add missing envelope markers expected by v1 clients, and buffer small stream fragments to avoid mid-frame splits.
- Adds a header-driven opt-in: clients may send "Prefer-Schema-Compat: transient-v1" to enable the shim for their session. No behavior changes for clients that do not set the header.
- Implements a streaming sanitizer that detects v2 frames with new typed fields (e.g., "tool_output.v2") and emits a v1-compatible envelope sequence (progress, tool_call, result) while preserving chunked transfer semantics.
- Adds telemetry counters and gauges: compat.request.enabled, compat.response.coercions, compat.buffered_fragments, and compat.deprecation_signals. These are tagged by model, route, and compatibility value.
- Documentation updates: docs/compatibility/schema-migration.md documents recommended client opt-in flow and migration checklist.

Implementation notes:
- The adapter lives in redwood-openai-compat so that behavior is isolated from core runtime. It exposes a small interface to allow runtime teams to opt into a deployable config.
- To avoid latency regressions we only buffer up to 256KB or 50ms of stream data (whichever comes first) and fall back to pass-through under heavy load. Buffer thresholds are configurable via env and per-tenant flags.
- Coercions are implemented as reversible transforms with telemetry emitted on any non-noop transform. This makes it possible to measure real usage and test for accidental data loss.

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/compat/adapter/adapter.go - core middleware and transform pipeline
- pkg/compat/transformers/stream_coercion.go - rules for v2->v1 envelope translation
- cmd/compat-proxy/main.go - wiring and feature-flag handling for header opt-in
- docs/compatibility/schema-migration.md - migration guide and examples
- integration-tests/compat/streaming_coercion_test.go - end-to-end streaming tests (mock client + proxy + runtime)
- telemetry/metrics_registry.go - added compat.* metrics and tags
- helm/values-compat.yaml - new config knobs for buffer sizes and opt-in policy
- pkg/compat/README.md - internal notes and troubleshooting

Commits summary:
- feat(adapter): initial transform pipeline and middleware scaffolding
- feat(transformers): v2->v1 streaming coercion rules + unit tests
- docs: add migration guide and opt-in examples
- test(integration): add streaming canary and flaky-case harness
- ci: add compat integration job to pipeline

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests: all new unit tests pass locally and on CI.
- Integration tests: the compat integration job exercised canary streams and passed on the second run after we addressed a timing race in the test harness. The PR includes a small stability fix for the harness.
- Load: synthetic local load showed <0.8ms added median latency for small messages when buffering disabled; worst-case 18ms for buffered cases within thresholds.

Review conversation (summary):
- Evan: "Nice, this looks well scoped. Two asks: make buffer thresholds tenant-configurable and ensure we never convert structured tool errors into success envelopes."
- Sana: "Added tenant config via helm/values-compat.yaml and added an explicit error-preservation check in stream_coercion.go. Unit tests added (see commit 3)."
- Diego: "We should also emit a specific deprecation telemetry counter so we can track when v2-only frames are seen from clients that didn't opt-in."
- Sana: "Added compat.deprecation_signals and surfaced it in metrics_registry.go. Also added a short section in docs describing the signal thresholds for automated deprecation windowing."
- Lydia: "Please add a short rollout plan and a kill-switch for the middleware in case of unforeseen regressions."
- Sana: "Added the kill-switch (COMPAT_ADAPTER_ENABLED=false) and documented the rollouts: feature-gate on main, canary in production for 48h on 10% of traffic, then gradual ramp. Added Linear tickets for the ramp schedule."
- Approvals: Evan, Diego, Lydia approved the final changes.

Rollout and backwards-compat strategy:
- Default off: shim is opt-in by header for the initial rollout so we don't change behavior for existing clients.
- Canary: deploy to compatibility proxy canary ring with adapter_enabled=true for 10% of internal traffic and all requests that include a migration-test header. Monitor compat.response.coercions and error rates.
- Metrics-driven retirement: once compat.deprecation_signals drops below threshold for 90 days and we have adoption metrics from linked Linear tasks, we will schedule removal of the shim.

Potential risks and mitigations:
- Latency increase under heavy buffering loads: mitigated by strict buffer caps and fallback to pass-through. Added e2e tests to exercise this.
- Silent data loss if transforms are incorrect: mitigated by conservative reversible transforms and explicit telemetry on any coercion.
- Unexpected client behavior for partially upgraded clients: kept opt-in header flow and documented recommended client migration steps.

Merge details:
- Merge method: squash and merge by Lydia Chen on 2026-03-03. Merge commit: "squash: transient schema adapter for streaming tool compatibility".
- Linear links attached to merge: ENG-3147, PM-522.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add server-side auto-opt-in for long-lived migrations once adoption metrics are clear (follow-up PR planned: feature/compat-auto-optin).
- Expand coercion rules to support typed-argument changes (planned).
- Add a small CLI tool to simulate v1 vs v2 streams for customer troubleshooting (RFC exists in PM-ldx).

If you want to run the adapter locally: see pkg/compat/README.md for an example curl invocation that sets the "Prefer-Schema-Compat: transient-v1" header and a small local runtime mock.
